transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, thank you. I suppose what brings me in is... I've just been living with this constant mix of guilt, fear, and anger. It's been like this ever since my friend was killed. Everyone seemed to think it would get better with time, but it just hasn't eased up the way they all thought it would.
How long ago was it that your friend was killed?
It's been... about two years and three months now. It happened while we were on a walking tour.
Since your friend's death, have you experienced intrusive memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about what happened, where it feels like you're re-living the event?

Yes, I do get those. It's... well, little things will just set it off. A crosswalk signal, or the growl of a heavy truck going by. Even just seeing a walking-tour map can suddenly put the whole scene right back in my head. It comes back so sharply that I can actually see my friend stepping off the curb again... right before I can stop it.
Since the accident, have you found yourself actively avoiding places, activities, or conversations that remind you of what happened—like avoiding walking tours or busy streets?

Yes, I do. I actually go out of my way to avoid that specific intersection entirely. And I've stopped signing up for most tours, or even local safety meetings. I just... I cannot bear the conversations when they circle back to what happened there. It's just easier to stay away from it all.
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually on edge, easily startled, or constantly watching for danger since the accident?

Yes, I definitely do. Whenever I'm anywhere near traffic, I just... I watch everything. Every truck, the curb, every single pedestrian. It feels like it is my responsibility to catch the danger before it happens again.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a qualifying traumatic stressor (witnessing the sudden violent death of a close friend) followed by a constellation of symptoms including intrusive re-experiencing (flashbacks, sensory-triggered memories), persistent avoidance of trauma-related cues (avoiding the intersection, tours, related conversations), and hyperarousal/hypervigilance (exaggerated scanning for danger, being easily triggered).
